Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Article 51
(1) Every organizer of an educational unit is obligated to provide opportunities for Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.
(2) Every organizer of an educational unit is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.
(3) In the event that a Child victim of Violence experiences dropping out of school, then the child victim of violence shall be provided formal or non-formal education, in this case carried out by the organizer of the educational unit and coordinated with UPTD PPA.

6.8.rationale: The judge relied on Pasal 32 about law enforcement and legal aid for women/children victims and witness protection. However, this is a general service component for handling cases (penegakan dan bantuan hukum) and does not necessarily constitute an 'intersectional approach' category of 'legal process involvement' as a distinct vulnerable group/context (e.g., women in detention, women offenders, or special protections for women involved in legal processes beyond being victims/witnesses). Since the regulation’s legal aid provisions are standard victim services, the golden label No is plausible for an intersectionality indicator, and the judge’s Yes reflects an overly broad reading.
